newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market quiet, China continues to buy.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market quiet, China continues to buy.

text.p: London's sugar freight market was subdued at the end of the week with the steady trickle of Chinese demand for Thai sugar about the only feature of interest, shipbrokers said on Friday.
Shipbrokers said Kerry Trading fixed 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to south China for mid-May and quoted for 3,000 tonnes of bagged sugar on the same route for May dates.
The timing and extent of Chinese demand has been the talk of physical sugar markets for many months.

Czarnikow was in the market for 14,200 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to Surabaya for prompt shipment, while E D & F Man quoted for 5/6,000 tonnes in bags from Santander to west Africa for the second half of May.
The only other firmer business came from Pacol, which was said to have fixed 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to the Black Sea for prompt shipment dates.
